newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo and the Kebble family's Consolidated Mining Corp Ltd have engineered an elaborate structure which tightens Khumalo's grip on the mining house.
- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's proposed change to the taxation of housing fringe benefits, anounced in his March budget, was rejected by parliament's finance committee on Tuesday.

- Retail and entertainement group CNA Gallo dropped headline earnings four percent to 85 million rand in the year to March as robust growth in entertainment was offset by the retail sector's disappointing performance.

- An Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd senior human resources manager and three Mouthpiece Workers' Union members have been suspended pending a disciplinary inquiry into their alleged actions when two National Union of Mineworkers members were tortured.
- Imports surged and exports were up slightly in April, yielding an anaemic trade surplus of 725 million rand after a bumper 1.98 billion in March.
- U.S. pharmaceutical companies have frozen new investments in South Africa pending the outcome of legislation on generic medicines.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The Mpumalanga provincial government has suspended the activitiies of the Mpumalanga Housing Board following allegations of irregularities in the awarding of a 190 million rand housing contract.
- Earnings from CNA Gallo's entertainment division exceeded those from retail for the first time, figures released on Tuesday indicated.
- Kairinos Foods will raise 148 million rand when it lists late next month.
- JCI was placed firmly in black hands on Tuesday through a series of transactions involving Brett Kebble's CMC, NK Properties and Witwatersrand Nigel.
SAKE BEELD
- Controversial health proposals from Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma have upset U.S. pharmaceutical firms who are displeased with her plans to promote generic medicines.
- South African imports grew faster than exports in April, causing the monthly trade surplus to fall to 725 million rand.
THE STAR
- Mpumalanga Premier Mathews Phosa has called on the auditor-general to investigate the 190 million rand housing project at the centre of a growing scandal.
- The ANC, the majority party in the Greater Johannesburg metropolitan council and its four substructures, announced on Tuesday there would be no rates increases this year.
